prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When tokens are loaded from TokenStorage (e.g. after a process restart), `token_expiry_time` is never set, so `is_token_valid()`/`can_refresh_token()` logic can't tell the token is actually expired. This causes stale, expired access tokens to be treated as valid and sent on requests instead of being proactively refreshed. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When tokens are loaded from TokenStorage (e.g. after a process restart), `token_expiry_time` is never set, so `is_token_valid()`/`can_refresh_token()` logic can't tell the token is actually expired. It's a 4-line change plus a matching `expired_tokens` test fixture. PR #2875 treats the same root cause as a symptom instead: it adds a new 'Step 3.5' branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler that attempts a stored-refresh-token exchange before falling back to full re-authorization, explicitly citing 'token_expiry_time never restored' as the reason. That's a larger, more invasive change to the request flow that becomes redundant once #1784 makes token_expiry_time correct on load — the proactive refresh path already in place would fire normally instead of requiring a reactive 401-triggered workaround.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Duplicate/reused in-flight JSON-RPC request ids collide in _request_streams, letting concurrent requests cross-wire responses or hang. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Duplicate/reused in-flight JSON-RPC request ids collide in _request_streams, letting concurrent requests cross-wire responses or hang. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a 409/400 guard rejecting an in-flight request id, but #3063 keys the guard with str(request_id), which collapses JSON-RPC ids 1 (int) and "1" (string) into the same key — causing a false-positive rejection or cross-wiring between an int id and a string id that the spec treats as distinct. #3221 introduces _request_stream_key(), which prefixes by type (i: vs s:) to preserve that distinction, and additionally prevents a string request id of "_GET_stream" from colliding with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY slot — an edge case #3063's diff does not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a 409/400 guard rejecting an in-flight request id, but #3063 keys the guard with str(request_id), which collapses JSON-RPC ids 1 (int) and "1" (string) into the same key — causing a false-positive rejection or cross-wiring between an int id and a string id that the spec treats as distinct. #3221 introduces _request_stream_key(), which prefixes by type (i: vs s:) to preserve that distinction, and additionally prevents a string request id of "_GET_stream" from colliding with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY slot — an edge case #3063's diff does not cover.
